controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Sets N0. It scales the result N(t) and the two bars of the amount vector in proportion, while lambda*t, the remaining fraction and the half-life T-half do not move.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Sets lambda. It changes the intermediate lambda*t, the remaining fraction exp(-lambda*t), the result N(t), the half-life T-half and the elapsed half-lives t/T-half; larger lambda means a faster decay and a shorter T-half.

controls.label: Elapsed time t
controls.help: Sets t. It changes the intermediate lambda*t, the remaining fraction, the result N(t) and the elapsed half-lives t/T-half, but it leaves the half-life T-half unchanged.

visuals.title: Remaining amount N(t) against elapsed time t
Remaining fraction exp(-lambda*t) against elapsed time t

explorations.title: Ten years at a slow decay constant
explorations.instruction: Predict: with N0 = 100 a.u. and lambda = 0.1 1/y, roughly what fraction of the nuclei is left after t = 10 y? Then apply the preset, which sets N0, lambda and t.
explorations.observe: The remaining fraction readout drops to about 0.368 and the remaining amount N(t) to about 36.8 a.u., while lambda*t reads exactly 1 and t/T-half reads about 1.44. The half-life readout stays at 6.93 y and the second bar of the amount chart is about a third of the first.
explorations.why: With lambda*t = 1 the exponent is exactly one decay time, so exp(-1) = 0.368 is the fraction left; multiplying by N0 = 100 a.u. gives N(t) = 36.8 a.u. The half-life is ln(2)/0.1 = 6.93 y, so 10 y is 1.44 half-lives, which is why more than half of the material is already gone.

explorations.title: Ten years at a fast decay constant
explorations.instruction: Predict: if lambda rises to 0.5 1/y but N0 and t stay the same, does the remaining amount fall by a factor of about 5 or by a much larger factor? Then apply the preset, which sets N0, lambda and t.
explorations.observe: The decay exponent lambda*t jumps to 5, the remaining fraction collapses to about 0.00674 and N(t) to about 0.674 a.u.; t/T-half rises to about 7.21 and the half-life readout falls to 1.39 y. The second bar in the amount chart becomes a thin sliver next to the first.
explorations.why: The remaining fraction is exp(-lambda*t), so the factor by which it shrinks is exp of the change in the exponent, not the ratio of the decay constants: raising the exponent from 1 to 5 multiplies the fraction by exp(-4) = 0.0183. The half-life ln(2)/lambda is five times shorter at 1.39 y, so the same 10 y now spans about 7.2 half-lives and only a few tenths of a percent of the material survives.

tests.name: at the start no time has passed
doubling N0 and lambda keeps the exponent at one and doubles the amount

invariants.name: remaining fraction lies between zero and one
decay exponent is nonnegative and bounded by lambda max times t max
remaining amount never exceeds the initial amount
half-life stays finite and inside its allowed range
